title: Azure Container Registry Overview
description: Understand Azure Container Registry (ACR) as the managed registry for storing and managing container images on Azure.

data.text: Azure Container Registry (ACR) is a managed, private registry for container images. It stores and manages your Docker and OCI images in Azure, providing geo-replication, vulnerability scanning, and integration with Azure services.

items: Private registry - images are accessible only to authorized users
Geo-replication - replicate images to multiple Azure regions
Image scanning - scan images for vulnerabilities using Microsoft Defender
Helm chart support - store Helm charts for Kubernetes deployments
Webhooks - trigger events on image push or delete

data.title: Azure CLI - Create an ACR Instance
data.content:
az acr create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --name myContainerRegistry \
  --sku Standard \
  --location eastus

data.title: Registry Name Rules
data.text: ACR registry names must be globally unique across all of Azure, contain only lowercase letters and numbers, and be 5-50 characters long.

terms.definition: A managed Docker-compatible registry service for storing and managing container images in Azure.
The pricing and performance tier of an ACR instance: Basic, Standard, or Premium.
The ability to replicate a registry to multiple Azure regions for low-latency image pulls worldwide.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ACR is Azure's managed container image registry
Integrates with AKS, App Service, and Functions
data.takeaway: ACR is the central hub for your container images in Azure.
